memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Let no yeast be found in your possession in all your land for seven days. Do not let any of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day remain until morning. - Deut 16:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The instructions get very specific. No yeast anywhere in the land for the whole week, and nothing of the Passover meal kept overnight. Why such care? Because God was teaching His people that their rescue was complete and that their obedience should be wholehearted, not half-kept.

Leaving meat until morning could tempt them toward carelessness or even a kind of hoarding, as though God's provision needed to be stretched by their own anxious planning. But the Passover was about trusting the God who had already delivered them. What He provided for that night was enough for that night.

We can learn to trust God like this, one day at a time. Jesus taught us to pray for "our daily bread," not a stockpile that lets us forget our need of Him (Matt 6:11). Clearing out the yeast pictures a life that refuses to let old sin quietly linger and spread. Sin, like yeast, works slowly and silently until it has touched everything. God's call to remove it entirely is not harshness, it is His care for our wholeness. Where is He inviting you to deal fully, and not partly, with something you have been tolerating?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to obey God only halfway?
2. What "small" sin have you been quietly tolerating?
3. How can you learn to trust God for today's provision?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me wholehearted obedience and daily trust. Help me not to tolerate any sin that spreads quietly in my heart. Amen.
